title: Nonlinear Multi-User Power-Bound Lifting
summary: Point-wise proximity lifts linear power bounds to dependent multi-user settings; extending it to nonlinear bounds while relaxing query-dependence conditions remains open.

formal_statement.body: A point-wise-proximity method converts single-user power bounds into multi-user power bounds and remains applicable when different users are dependent, for example through a shared primitive. The method currently requires the power bound to be linear and imposes nontrivial conditions on how the bound depends on the number of queries. Extend single-user-to-multi-user power-bound lifting to nonlinear power bounds and, ideally, remove or weaken these query-dependence conditions while preserving applicability to dependent users.

scope.domain: Information-theoretic security: lifting single-user power bounds to dependent multi-user settings via point-wise proximity.
assumptions: The current power bound is linear.
The power bound's dependence on the number of queries satisfies nontrivial conditions.
parameters: Number of queries — the variable whose influence on the bound is subject to nontrivial conditions
scope.unresolved_remainder: Extend the lifting method to nonlinear power bounds and, ideally, remove or weaken its query-dependence conditions while retaining applicability to dependent users.

progress.summary: The source presents a lifting method that accommodates dependencies among users, then highlights its linearity and query-dependence requirements as limitations framing a broader lifting challenge.
citation_labels: Tim Beyne et al., Information-theoretic security with asymmetries
